newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on primary rate fears.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on primary rate fears.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed up 40 basis points to 20.10 percent on Wednesday on what traders said was market feeling that primary rates had fallen too far and would soon rise again.
"They didn't like the fall in short-term Cetes rates, so some dealers stepped in to sell and take profits feeling rates could not fall any further," a trader said.
Benchmark 28-day Cetes rates plummeted 176 basis points to 19.69 percent at Tuesday night's primary auction, their lowest level since the December 1994 peso devaluation crisis.
Traders noted that ample market liquidity reined in the increase in overnight rates, and said this was partly due to capital inflows from abroad due to a stable peso.
"Even though the central bank continues to drain liquidity, the market is still awash with money, which keeps rates down and will continue to do so as long as the peso is stable," a dealer said.
Banco de Mexico offset surplus liquidity today by draining 1.191 billion pesos from the market through three auctions.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 0.45 of a centavo firmer at 7.7840/7.7890 per dollar.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed unchanged at 21.70 percent.
Despite some brokers' fears that the sharp fall in primary rates may have been premature, others saw the move as helping to kick-start the economy.

"The central bank appears to be seeking to revive credit and raise consumption. Inflation looks like it's going to be on the low side in the coming months and there is scope for interest rates to fall further," another dealer said.
Liquidity of 1.944 billion pesos was scheduled to enter to the market on Thursday. Nonetheless, traders said liquidity could be pinched by demand for cash ahead of the weekend and to pay wage bills.
